units.quote: An applicant with a pending name change must not be issued a passport in her/his new name.
scope_quotes: c. The court order or decree must be final:
units.meaning: Under the rule that a court order or decree must be final, a passport must not be issued in the new name to an applicant whose name change is pending.

units.quote: See 8 FAM 1001.5 regarding applying for a replacement passport in a new name;
scope_quotes: c. The court order or decree must be final:
(1) An applicant with a pending name change must not be issued a passport in her/his new name.
units.meaning: Cross-reference providing informational guidance to consult 8 FAM 1001.5 regarding applying for a replacement passport in a new name.

units.quote: An applicant with a pending name change must not be issued a form FS-240 in her/his new name.
scope_quotes: c. The court order or decree must be final:
units.meaning: Under the rule that a court order or decree must be final, a Form FS-240 must not be issued in the new name to an applicant whose name change is pending.

units.quote: See 8 FAM 1001.3 regarding amending a form FS-240; and
scope_quotes: c. The court order or decree must be final:
(2) An applicant with a pending name change must not be issued a form FS-240 in her/his new name.
units.meaning: Cross-reference providing informational guidance to consult 8 FAM 1001.3 regarding amending a Form FS-240.

units.quote: You must clear the applicant's pending name even though the name change is not final and even if the passport is not being issued at this time.
scope_quotes: c. The court order or decree must be final:
units.meaning: Personnel are required to clear the applicant's pending name regardless of whether the name change is final and regardless of whether the passport is being issued at the present time.

units.quote: The court order or decree must list both the applicant's current and former name(s).
units.meaning: A court order or decree submitted for a name change is required to list both the applicant's current name and former name(s).

units.quote: You may receive a court order in which the applicant's former name is made confidential (e.g., California's Safe at Home program).
scope_quotes: d. The court order or decree must list both the applicant's current and former name(s).
units.meaning: States the scenario/exception trigger where a court order renders the applicant's former name confidential (such as under California's Safe at Home program).

units.quote: When this occurs, the applicant must provide both her/his current and former names on the application.
scope_quotes: d. The court order or decree must list both the applicant's current and former name(s).
EXCEPTION: You may receive a court order in which the applicant's former name is made confidential (e.g., California's Safe at Home program).
units.meaning: When an applicant provides a court order with a confidential former name, the applicant is required to provide both their current and former names on the passport application.

units.quote: You may request additional evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality or identity in accordance with 22 CFR 51.23 and 22 CFR 51.45.
scope_quotes: d. The court order or decree must list both the applicant's current and former name(s).
EXCEPTION: You may receive a court order in which the applicant's former name is made confidential (e.g., California's Safe at Home program).
units.meaning: In confidential former name court order situations, personnel are permitted to request additional evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality or identity pursuant to 22 CFR 51.23 and 22 CFR 51.45.

units.quote: 8 FAM 403.1-3(B) Name Spacing
units.meaning: Section heading for guidance on name spacing, conveying no substantive operational rule.
Administrative publication and revision metadata with no substantive operational rule.

units.quote: In accordance with International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) recommendations, U.S. passports, form FS-240, and form DS-2060 are printed in all uppercase letters.
units.meaning: Explains that U.S. passports, Form FS-240, and Form DS-2060 are printed in all uppercase letters following ICAO recommendations.

units.quote: Printing a name with multiple parts in uppercase letters causes the name to appear as one word unless the parts are separated with spaces.
units.meaning: Explains the technical consequence that multipart names printed in uppercase appear as a single word unless separated by spaces.

units.quote: Consequently, if the applicant has a name with multiple parts, you must determine how the name will appear:
units.meaning: If an applicant has a multipart name, personnel are obligated to determine how the name will appear on the document.

units.quote: If the applicant's previous passport had a space, you should add a space on the current application;
scope_quotes: Consequently, if the applicant has a name with multiple parts, you must determine how the name will appear:
units.meaning: When determining the appearance of a multipart name, if the applicant's previous passport contained a space, personnel are advised to add a space on the current application.

units.quote: If the applicant does not have a previous passport and the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality or ID has a space, you should add a space on the current application; or
scope_quotes: Consequently, if the applicant has a name with multiple parts, you must determine how the name will appear:
units.meaning: When determining the appearance of a multipart name, if the applicant lacks a prior passport but their citizenship/nationality evidence or ID has a space, personnel are advised to add a space on the current application.

units.quote: If the applicant expresses a clear preference to add or remove space, either verbally or in writing, you may add or remove it per the applicant's preference.
scope_quotes: Consequently, if the applicant has a name with multiple parts, you must determine how the name will appear:
units.meaning: When determining the appearance of a multipart name, personnel are authorized to add or remove space in accordance with the applicant's stated preference if the applicant communicates a clear preference verbally or in writing.

units.quote: NOTE: If you receive applications from several family members, you should space the last names consistently, unless a family member expresses a clear preference for a different spacing.
units.meaning: When receiving applications from multiple family members, personnel should space their last names consistently, except when an individual family member explicitly expresses a preference for different spacing.

units.quote: NOTE: For special-issuance passports, the spacing of an eligible family member's last name should match the spacing of the last name of the sponsor.
units.meaning: In the case of special-issuance passports, the spacing of an eligible family member's last name should correspond to the spacing of the sponsor's last name.

units.quote: Name spacing issues are generally not sufficient cause to rewrite a passport, unless the Department disregarded the applicant's clear preference (see 8 FAM 1001.2).
units.meaning: Issues regarding name spacing generally do not justify rewriting a passport, except when the Department failed to follow the applicant's clearly expressed preference.

units.quote: Arabic ordinal numbers must be changed to Roman numerals, for example, 2nd to II, 3rd to III:
units.meaning: Personnel are required to convert Arabic ordinal numbers in names to Roman numerals (e.g., changing '2nd' to 'II' and '3rd' to 'III').

units.quote: Some applicants may include the prefix “Sr.” as an abbreviation for “Señor” in Spanish meaning “Mr.” or “Mister” in English.
units.meaning: Explains that certain applicants use the prefix 'Sr.' to represent the Spanish title 'Señor' ('Mr.' or 'Mister').

units.quote: If you determine that this is the case, follow the guidance in 8 FAM 403.1-5(C) regarding ranks and titles.
scope_quotes: d. Some applicants may include the prefix “Sr.” as an abbreviation for “Señor” in Spanish meaning “Mr.” or “Mister” in English.
units.meaning: If personnel determine that 'Sr.' is used as an abbreviation for 'Señor' rather than a suffix, they must follow the instructions in 8 FAM 403.1-5(C) covering ranks and titles.

units.quote: Name suffix issues are generally not sufficient cause to rewrite a passport, unless the Department disregarded the applicant's clear preference (see 8 FAM 1001.2).
units.meaning: Name suffix issues are generally not considered sufficient reason to rewrite a passport, except in cases where the Department ignored the applicant's clearly stated preference.
